items.title: Julie’s Journey: Navigating breast cancer treatment with support of caregivers
items.description: Now two years since completing her chemotherapy and in remission, Julie’s story is a testament to the strength and resilience of women facing breast cancer.

items.title: Pickleball Safety 101: Expert tips to Keep You in the game
items.description: Use these few tweaks to help keep you from getting in a real pickle on the court.

items.title: New Technology Helps Keep Breast Cancer from Coming Back
items.description: With the help of new technology, doctors can find and treat the stray cancer cells that make cancer come back.

items.title: Breaking Down Stigma and Building Awareness Around Mental Health
items.description: Mental illness is common. Nearly one in five Americans have mental illness. Clint Thurgood, director of Crisis Service at Intermountain Healthcare talks about why it’s important to talk openly about our mental health and how we can work together to overcome the stigma around mental health.

items.title: A Better Way of Doing Prostate Screening
items.description: Prostate cancer is the leading type of cancer among Utah men, and Utah has one of the highest incidents of prostate cancer in the country. Addressing this issue is a priority, so how do we detect prostate cancer early and make sure patients have the best outcomes possible?

items.title: 7 Misconceptions About Midwives
items.description: Midwives have been caring for women for centuries. But until the 1940s, history tells us they were generally local women with good hearts and instincts, but no formal education. Times have changed, as has the scope of midwifery practice.

items.title: 6 Tips to Better Manage Your Stress
items.description: In today’s society, more and more people are dealing with stress. It has become increasingly important to find ways to manage stress as it is shown to have a direct relation to your heart’s health.

items.title: 5 Misconceptions About Mammograms
items.description: Many misconceptions exist about mammograms, but the fact is mammograms can impact your long-term health — and save your life.
